jen: customer reported a 429 burst right after their monthly credits should've refilled (midnight PST). UI shows full monthly bucket but their API calls were getting `429` for ~15m. Any quick triage steps? :thinking:

alejandro: can you paste the org id and a sample request/response? is this via streaming websocket or normal REST?

jen: org=acme-inc-42, REST generate endpoint. Customer sent this repro: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED' \
  -H 'X-Org-ID: acme-inc-42' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-1","input":"hello"}'
```
response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
Body: `{"error":"quota_exhausted","detail":"monthly tokens exhausted"}`
They say the console shows 100% of monthly quota at 00:00 but API 429s started at 00:02 and stopped around 00:18.

maya: first-pass theory — display cache vs billing topup ordering. UI cache may be updated by a different path that gets the freshly computed topup earlier than the API quota/ratelimit TTL is cleared. Also check if their tenant timezone != PST (we run topup job in UTC rollover windows). Did they recently change plan or have a prorate?

alejandro: +1. Also ask them for request-id from the 429 response headers (x-request-id / x-rw-trace) and any `X-RateLimit-*` headers. If we have the request id we can look up the serving logs and the quota service ledger at that time.

jen: customer provided trace: `rwd-trace-0001-abc`. No plan change. They said they had a long-running websocket session before midnight and then issued many small REST calls after reconnect.

maya: long-running sessions can hold in-flight token accounting or interact poorly with burst windows. If the streaming session had retries, it can consume burst quota. Also our cache invalidation for the per-tenant rate limiter has a 60s staleness window in the control plane — if topup job and cache TTL race, API will still enforce the old 0 credits until invalidation.

sam: action items: 1) Support: ask customer to attach `x-request-id` and a short timeline. 2) Eng/Infra: check the topup job run at ~00:00 UTC and the quota-service cache invalidation logs for `acme-inc-42` between 00:00–00:20. 3) DevEx: send a short retry guidance snippet (exp backoff + check X-RateLimit headers).

deploy-bot: rollout note: billing-cache-invalidation-fix deployed to canary @2026-03-02T00:16Z by ci/billing-team (sha: b4f2c1) :rocket:

alejandro: also recommend immediate mitigation for customer: if they can switch to a dedicated key/route (short-lived burst quota) or pause aggressive reconnects for 10-20m while cache settles. Provided sample retry policy: 
```
1) on 429: sleep 500ms * 2^attempts, max 10s
2) if still 429 after 3 retries return soft-failure and alert support
3) log x-request-id + timestamp
```

jen: replied to customer with steps, asked for x-request-id + timestamp window and suggested the retry policy. Customer will try and report back. Closing for now unless we see reproduction on our side. :thumbsup:
